exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 2x2 Matrix

question.text:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by

\[ L =\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

\[ \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y} \end{cases} \] is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*} This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = 5 \\ -7y_1+ y_2 = -2. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $y_1=5$ and $y_2=33.$

Therefore, $\mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 33 \end{bmatrix}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix

question.text:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by \[ L = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1& 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

\[ \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y} \end{cases} \]

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ y_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}. \]

This gives the system of equations

\[ \begin{cases} y_1 = 6 \\ -y_1+y_2 = -2 \\ y_1 - y_2 + y_3 = 0. \end{cases} \]

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

\begin{align*} y_1 &= 6,\\[7pt] y_2 &= -2+y_1 \\[3pt] &=-2+6 \\[3pt] &=4,\\[7pt] y_3 &= -y_1+y_2 \\[3pt] &=-(6)+4 \\[3pt] &=-2. \end{align*}

Therefore, $ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}. $

example.title: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix

question.text:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by

\[ L= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -5 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -3 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

\[ \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y} \end{cases} \]

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ y_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -3 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix}. \]

This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = -1 \\ -2y_1+y_2 = -3 \\ 8y_1 -5y_2 + y_3 = 8. \end{cases} \]

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

\begin{align*} y_1 &=-1, \\[7pt] y_2 &= -3+2y_1 \\[3pt] &=-3+2(-1) \\[3pt] &=-5, \\[7pt] y_3 &= 8-8y_1+5y_2 \\[3pt] &=8-8(-1)+5(-5) \\[3pt] &=-9. \end{align*}

Therefore, $ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -5 \\ -9 \end{bmatrix}. $

example.title: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix

question.text:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by \[ L = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

\[ \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y} \end{cases} \]

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ y_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}. \]

This gives the system of equations

\[ \begin{cases} y_1 = 1 \\ -2y_1+y_2 = -2 \\ -y_1 + y_2 + y_3 = 2. \end{cases} \]

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

\begin{align*} y_1 &= 1, \\[7pt] y_2 &= -2+2y_1 \\[3pt] &=-2+2(1) \\[3pt] &=0,\\[7pt] y_3 &= 2+y_1-y_2 \\[3pt] &=2+(1)-(0) \\[3pt] &=3. \end{align*}

Therefore, $ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. $

example.title: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix

question.text:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by

\[ L= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 9 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

\[ \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y} \end{cases} \]

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 9 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ y_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = -2 \\ 9y_1+y_2 = -2 \\ -4y_1 +y_2 + y_3 = 1. \end{cases} \]

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

\begin{align*} y_1 &=-2, \\[7pt] y_2 &= -2-9y_1 \\[3pt] &=-2-9(-2) \\[3pt] &=16, \\[7pt] y_3 &= 1+4y_1-y_2 \\[3pt] &=1+4(-2)-(16) \\[3pt] &=-23. \end{align*}

Therefore, $ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 16 \\ -23 \end{bmatrix}. $

question.text:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by

\[ L= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ 7 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

\[ \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y} \end{cases} \]

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

\[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ y_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ 7 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = 9 \\ 7y_1+y_2 = 7 \\ -9y_1 + y_3 = -1. \end{cases} \]

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

\begin{align*} y_1 &=9, \\[7pt] y_2 &= 7-7y_1 \\[3pt] &=7-7(9) \\[3pt] &=-56, \\[7pt] y_3 &= -1+9y_1 \\[3pt] &=-1+9(9) \\[3pt] &=80. \end{align*}

Therefore, $ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ -56 \\ 80 \end{bmatrix}. $

exampleAnswers.title: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization

question.text: Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by \[ A = \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{L} \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}}_{U}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}. \] If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 \cdot y_1?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

  • First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}y_1 \\y_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = -4\\ -y_1+y_2 = -1. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $y_1=-4$ and $y_2=-5.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\-5\end{bmatrix}. \]

  • Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} x_1+x_2 = -4 \\ 2x_2 = -5. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $x_2=-\dfrac{5}{2}$ and $x_1=-\dfrac{3}{2}.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{3}{2} \\ -\dfrac{5}{2} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Finally, $x_1\cdot y_1 = \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \cdot (-4) = 6.$

question.text: Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by \[ A = \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{L} \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}}_{U}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 \cdot y_1?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

  • First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}y_1 \\y_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = 3\\ -2y_1+y_2 = -3. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $y_1=3$ and $y_2=3.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \]

  • Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} x_1+3x_2 = 3 \\ 2x_2 = 3. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $x_2=\dfrac 3 2$ and $x_1=-\dfrac{3}{2}.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{3}{2} \\ \dfrac 3 2 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Finally, $x_1 \cdot y_1 = -\dfrac{3}{2} \cdot 3 = -\dfrac 92.$

question.text: Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by \[ A = \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{L} \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 8 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{U}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 + y_2?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

  • First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}y_1 \\y_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = 4 \\ -y_1+y_2 = 1. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $y_1=4$ and $y_2=5.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}. \]

  • Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 8 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} 8x_1-4x_2 = 4 \\ x_2 = 5. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $x_2=5$ and $x_1=3.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Finally, $x_1 + y_2 = 3 + 5= 8.$

example.title: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization

question.text: Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by \[ A = \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{L} \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}}_{U}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 20 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_2 \cdot y_2?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

  • First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}y_1 \\y_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 20 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = 6 \\ 4y_1+y_2 = 20. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $y_1=6$ and $y_2=-4.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}. \]

  • Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} 2x_1-x_2 = 6 \\ 4x_2 = -4. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $x_2=-1$ and $x_1=\dfrac 5 2.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac 5 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Finally, $x_2 \cdot y_2 = \left(-1\right) \cdot (-4) = 4.$

example.title: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization

question.text: Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by \[ A = \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}}_{L} \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}}_{U}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}. \] If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 \cdot y_2?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

\begin{align*} A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \underbrace{(LU)}_{A} \mathbf{x}= \mathbf{b}. \end{align*}

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

\[ L \underbrace{(U \mathbf{x})}_{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} \\ U\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{y}. \end{cases} \]

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

  • First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}y_1 \\y_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y_1 = -3 \\ 3y_1+y_2 = -7. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $y_1=-3$ and $y_2=2.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}. \]

  • Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get \[ \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{y}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}. \] This gives the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} 4x_1+x_2 = -3 \\ 2x_2 = 2. \end{cases} \] The solution to this system is $x_2=1$ and $x_1=-1.$ Therefore, \[ \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Finally, $x_1 \cdot y_2 = (-1) \cdot 2 = -2.$
